questions.question_text:
The energy required to remove an electron from the highest occupied atomic orbital is known as
(A) Ionization energy
(B) Kinetic energy
(C) Binding energy
(D) Vibrational energy
questions.answer:
(A) Ionization energy
Explanation: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove the most loosely held electron from the outermost shell of an atom.

questions.question_text:
The most electronegative element possess which of the following the electronic configuration?
(A) ns2 np2
(B) ns2 np4
(C) ns2 np5
(D) ns2 np3
questions.answer:
(C) ns2 np5
Explanation: Elements with ns2 np5 configuration include fluorine, the most electronegative element.

questions.question_text:
Identify the least stable ion amongst the following:
(A) Li+
(B) Be-
(C) B-
(D) C-
questions.answer:
(B) Be-
Explanation: Be- is highly unstable due to the unfavorable addition of an electron to an already filled 2s orbital.

questions.question_text:
The property Atomic size in the periodic table _______ on moving down a group
(A) Gradually increases
(B) Gradually decreases
(C) Increase then decrease
(D) Decrease then increase
questions.answer:
(A) Gradually increases
Explanation: Atomic size increases down a group due to addition of new shells.

questions.question_text:
Loss of small molecule from original organic molecule is
(A) Addition reaction
(B) Elimination reaction
(C) Substitution reaction
(D) Reduction reaction
questions.answer:
(B) Elimination reaction
Explanation: Elimination reactions involve removal of a small molecule (like H2O, HX) from the reactant.

questions.question_text:
Drugs that are used to diagnose, cure and prevent disease are called
(A) Additive drugs
(B) Industrial drugs
(C) Pharmaceutical drugs
(D) Single cell drugs
questions.answer:
(C) Pharmaceutical drugs
Explanation: Pharmaceutical drugs are medicines used for treatment, diagnosis, or prevention of diseases.
questions.chapter: Unit 3: Synthesis of a commonly used drug molecule

questions.question_text:
The most suitable reagent for the following transformation is
[Image: Cyclohexene -> Adipic acid (HOOC-(CH2)4-COOH)]
(A) KMnO4
(B) OsO4
(C) K2Cr2O7
(D) PCC
questions.answer:
(A) KMnO4
Explanation: Hot acidic KMnO4 causes oxidative cleavage of double bonds, converting cyclohexene to adipic acid.
questions.chapter: Unit 3: Introduction to reactions involving oxidation/ring openings

questions.question_text:
Identify the reducing agent from the following
(A) OsO4
(B) PCC
(C) LiAlH4
(D) K2Cr2O7
questions.answer:
(C) LiAlH4
Explanation: LiAlH4 is a strong reducing agent commonly used in organic chemistry for reduction reactions.
questions.chapter: Unit 3: Introduction to reactions involving reduction

questions.question_text:
Which of the following method is used to remove hardness from water sample.
(A) Desalination
(B) Decarbonation
(C) Demineralization
(D) Distillation
questions.answer:
(C) Demineralization
Explanation: Demineralization (or ion exchange) removes all dissolved minerals, including ions causing hardness.

questions.question_text:
The exhausted cationic resins are regenerated by
(A) Soft water
(B) Acid
(C) Alkali
(D) NaCl
questions.answer:
(B) Acid
Explanation: Cation exchange resins are regenerated by washing with acid, which restores the H+ sites.

questions.question_text:
Permanent hardness of water is due to calcium
(A) Chlorides
(B) Bicarbonates
(C) Nitrates
(D) Acetates
questions.answer:
(A) Chlorides
Explanation: Permanent hardness is caused by chlorides and sulphates of calcium/magnesium, which do not decompose on boiling.

questions.question_text:
Water can be sterilized by
(A) CCl4
(B) Cl2
(C) CaCO3
(D) NaOH
questions.answer:
(B) Cl2
Explanation: Chlorine is commonly used as a disinfectant in water treatment to kill bacteria and pathogens.

questions.question_text:
Hypophosphite is used as a reducing agent in
(A) Electro plating
(B) Electroless plating
(C) Hot dipping
(D) Etching
questions.answer:
(B) Electroless plating
Explanation: Hypophosphite acts as the reducing agent in electroless plating, facilitating metal deposition without electricity.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following metal will form non-porous oxide layer?
(A) Na
(B) K
(C) Al
(D) Sr
questions.answer:
(C) Al
Explanation: Aluminium forms a non-porous, protective oxide layer that prevents further corrosion.

questions.question_text:
Anhydrous inorganic metal surface in the absence of moisture exhibits
(A) Wet corrosion
(B) Dry corrosion
(C) Galvanic corrosion
(D) Pitting corrosion
questions.answer:
(B) Dry corrosion
Explanation: Dry corrosion occurs in absence of moisture, typically due to direct reaction with atmospheric gases.

questions.question_text:
When the hydrogen over voltage is low, the corrosion rate will be
(A) High
(B) Low
(C) Independent
(D) Zero
questions.answer:
(A) High
Explanation: A low hydrogen overvoltage facilitates hydrogen evolution and thus increases corrosion rate.

questions.question_text:
Nernst glower is the source of
(A) UV-Visible radiation
(B) IR radiation
(C) Microwave
(D) Radiowave
questions.answer:
(B) IR radiation
Explanation: Nernst glower is a source used for producing infrared radiation in spectroscopy instruments.

questions.question_text:
Reference electrode used in potentiometric titration is
(A) Platinum electrode
(B) Hydrogen electrode
(C) Glass electrode
(D) Calomel electrode
questions.answer:
(D) Calomel electrode
Explanation: Calomel electrode is a very common reference electrode due to its stable and reproducible potential.

questions.question_text:
Finger print region in IR spectroscopy is ____
(A) 4000 - 1400 cm-1
(B) 3600 - 3200 cm-1
(C) 1400 - 900 cm-1
(D) 2850 - 2969 cm-1
questions.answer:
(C) 1400 - 900 cm-1
Explanation: The fingerprint region of IR spectra is from 1400 to 900 cm-1, unique for each molecule.

questions.question_text:
Hydrogen bonding in a molecule can be detected easily using.
(A) Flame emission spectroscopy
(B) Atomic absorption spectroscopy
(C) UV-visible spectroscopy
(D) IR spectroscopy
questions.answer:
(D) IR spectroscopy
Explanation: IR spectroscopy is very sensitive to vibrations affected by hydrogen bonding in molecules.
